Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{9}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{9}^{4}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{9}(4f(x)+2)\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{4}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{4}^{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(-6)+2\cdot x\,{|}_{4}^{9} \\  & =-24+2(9-4) \\  & =-24+10 \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$
